name: jms-client
description: Run commands, transfer files and browse assets on a JumpServer v4 bastion from your AI assistant.
long_description:
Access the assets behind a [JumpServer v4](https://docs.jumpserver.org/zh/v4/) bastion host: list what you are authorized to reach, run commands, and move files over SFTP.

Connections are pooled, so one login serves many commands instead of re-authenticating per call. A server may define both an internal and an external address, and the tool picks whichever is reachable, so the same configuration works inside and outside the office network.

Credentials are never written to the configuration file: the password and TOTP secret live in the operating system credential store (Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain, or Linux Secret Service). Run `jms config add <alias>` once to store them.

Everything the assistant executes is also written to a local JSONL audit stream, which you can follow with `jms tail` or join interactively with `jms attach`.

tools.name: jms_ls
tools.description: List or search authorized assets on a JumpServer.

tools.name: jms_resolve_asset
tools.description: Resolve an asset to its connection info (address, account, protocol).

tools.name: jms_exec
tools.description: Execute a command on an asset and return its output.

tools.name: jms_sftp_upload
tools.description: Upload a local file to an asset via SFTP.

tools.name: jms_sftp_download
tools.description: Download a file from an asset to the local machine via SFTP.

tools.name: jms_sftp_relay
tools.description: Relay a file between two assets (streamed, no local disk).

tools.name: jms_config_list
tools.description: List configured JumpServer servers, marking the default with '*'.
